content: 1. The coadministration of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may lead to an increase in the plasma concentrations of ivosidenib, which can elevate the risk of QTc interval prolongation. It is essential to monitor for this increased risk. 2. Metronidazole can elevate the levels or effects of ixabepilone by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 3. The combination of bismuth subsalicylate and labetalol may result in pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor the patient. This interaction may block renal prostaglandin synthesis, potentially causing severe hypertension. 4. Lanthanum carbonate reduces tetracycline levels by binding cations in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer oral tetracycline antibiotics at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum. This interaction applies only to oral tetracyclines. 5. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 6. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 7. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Additionally, monitor for adverse effects if lefamulin is coadministered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 8. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of tetracycline by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Lenacapavir may also increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after its last subcutaneous dose, potentially raising the risk of adverse reactions. 9. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine, potentially necessitating dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. 10. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine, potentially requiring dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. 11. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of oral levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor the patient. 12. Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of oral levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor the patient. Antibiotics may reduce hormonal contraceptive efficacy. 13. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 14. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of tetracycline by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 15. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of loratadine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 16. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of losartan by affecting hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This may inhibit the conversion of losartan to its active metabolite E-3174. The clinical significance of this interaction is not established; monitor the therapeutic response to determine losartan dosage. 17. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day. 18. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. If coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day. 19. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 20. Magnesium supplements decrease tetracycline levels by forming an insoluble complex, reducing drug absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer magnesium 2 hours before or 4 hours after tetracycline. 21. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 22. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a reduced mavacamten dose. 23. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Monitor for adverse effects if mavorixafor is coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. If necessary, reduce the daily mavorixafor dose. 24. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Monitor for adverse effects if mavorixafor is coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. If necessary, reduce the daily mavorixafor dose. 25. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. 26. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 27. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. 28. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of mestranol by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. 29. Tetracycline decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor the patient. 30. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of methadone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 31. Tetracycline increases methotrexate levels by decreasing its elimination. Use caution and monitor the patient. If tetracyclines cannot be avoided in patients receiving high-dose methotrexate, closely monitor methotrexate plasma concentrations and patients for signs and symptoms of toxicity. 32. Methoxsalen and tetracycline may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Additive photosensitizing effects may occur. 33. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 34. Bismuth subsalicylate decreases the levels or effects of intranasal metoclopramide by impairing gastrointestinal motility, which may reduce systemic absorption of metoclopramide. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effect. 35. Bismuth subsalicylate and metoprolol may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor the patient. This interaction may block renal prostaglandin synthesis, potentially causing severe hypertension. 36. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of midazolam by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 37. Mipomersen and tetracycline may increase each other's toxicity. Both drugs have the potential to elevate hepatic enzymes; monitor liver function tests (LFTs). 38. Mitotane decreases tetracycline levels by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Mitotane is a strong inducer of cytochrome P450 3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. 39. Bismuth subsalicylate and nadolol may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor the patient. This interaction may block renal prostaglandin synthesis, potentially causing severe hypertension. 40. Nafcillin decreases tetracycline levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 41. Tetracycline increases naldemedine levels by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 42. Metronidazole increases naldemedine levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Monitor naldemedine for potential adverse effects if coadministered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 43. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of nateglinide by influencing hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 44. Bismuth subsalicylate and nebivolol may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor the patient. This interaction may block renal prostaglandin synthesis, potentially causing severe hypertension. 45. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, raising the risk of adverse effects. 46. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 47. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 48. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 49. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of nisoldipine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 50. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, raising the risk of adverse effects. 51. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 52. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 53. Bismuth subsalicylate decreases the levels or effects of oral omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral form of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Separate the dosing of tetracyclines from these products. 54. Ondansetron and metronidazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient. Exercise caution if metronidazole is coadministered with intravenous ondansetron or a higher intravenous ondansetron dose (do not exceed 16 mg IV). 55. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 56. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 57. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Avoid coadministration of palovarotene, a CYP3A substrate, with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 58. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Avoid coadministration of palovarotene, a CYP3A substrate, with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palovarotene dose by 50%. 59. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of parecoxib by influencing hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 60. Bismuth subsalicylate and penbutolol may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor the patient. This interaction may block renal prostaglandin synthesis, potentially causing severe hypertension. 61. Bismuth subsalicylate and pindolol may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor the patient. This interaction may block renal prostaglandin synthesis, potentially causing severe hypertension. 62. Tetracycline decreases the effects of piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 63. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Avoid coadministration of pazopanib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors if possible; if coadministration is necessary, decrease the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 64. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of phenytoin by affecting hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 65. Polycarbophil decreases tetracycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral form of both agents. Use caution and monitor the patient. 66. Tetracycline and porfimer may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Enhanced photosensitivity may occur. 67. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of prednisone by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 68. Bismuth subsalicylate and propranolol may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor the patient. This interaction may block renal prostaglandin synthesis, potentially causing severe hypertension. 69. Metronidazole increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 70.
